Colombo Port records 10% growth in transshipment volumes
The Port of Colombo recorded a 10% increase in transshipment volumes during the first ten months of 2026 compared with the same period last year. Throughput rose from 5,825,909 twenty-foot equivalent units (TEUs) between January and October 2025 to 6,406,363 TEUs during the corresponding period in 2026. This represents an increase of 580,454 TEUs.Reflecting this sustained growth, the Port of Colombo advanced to 20th place among the world’s busiest container ports in the first half of 2026, according to the latest Alphaliner rankings, moving up from 26th place at the end of 2025.

Banks’ appetite to lend cools as loan demand rises: CBSL survey
Sri Lanka’s banks became markedly more cautious about lending in the third quarter even as demand for loans picked up, the Central Bank’s latest Credit Supply Survey showed. Their outlook for the final quarter points to a wider gap between the two. The survey comes ahead of the Central Bank’s monetary policy announcement this Friday (20).Overall willingness to lend fell to 27.4 in the third quarter from 40.4 in the second. The reading is still positive, so willingness rose, but at a much slower pace. The slowdown showed up in retail (38.0 from 52.0), corporate (41.4 from 43.9) and SME lending (25.3 from 27.8).

Sri Lanka Customs achieves over 59-pct of November 2026 target in 16 days
Revenue collected by Sri Lanka Customs in the first 15 days of November accounted for over 59 percent of the month’s target, official data showed, with the island nation poised to see a fresh record high revenue this year.
The revenue collecting body has surpassed monthly targets for 10 straight months through October.Customs has set a revenue target of 2,207 billion rupees for this year, 13.5 percent less than last year as it expects a significant decline in car imports. However, it has already achieved 2,456.8 1 billion rupees through November 16.

SLT-Mobitel to upkeep institution-matched salaries
With ambitions to invest in its workforce, Sri Lankan telecommunications State-owned enterprise SLT-Mobitel is to continue to pay its employees recently institution-matched salaries – which is likely to cost a ‘few billions’ each year, according to Chairperson Mothilal de Silva. He made these comments speaking at an event announcing the company’s financial performance on Tuesday (18).According to its Q3 financials, the Group’s profit after tax during the first 9 months of the year increased by 59.4% to Rs 10.03 billion, with a revenue growth of 11.1%.

Fitch thumbs up for Budget
Fitch Ratings yesterday gave Budget 2027 a major vote of confidence, saying it signals the Government’s ongoing commitment to fiscal discipline and debt reduction while accommodating higher spending on investment and cyclone reconstruction.“Fiscal discipline, demonstrated again by the outperformance of fiscal targets in 2026, and a focus on debt reduction were key factors behind our upgrade of the sovereign rating to ‘B-‌’/Stable from ‘CCC+’ in September,” the rating agency said in a statement yesterday.

Anthropic clinches biggest IPO ever with $81 billion offering
Reuters was first to report earlier that IPO was upsized by about 19% to 980 million shares from its initial plan to sell 825 million shares at between $70 and $78 apiece. Anthropic is also raising $26 billion through a private placement at the IPO price, the filings show. On a fully diluted basis, the IPO values the company at about $1.5 trillion including securities such as stock options and restricted stock.

Anthropic, the first major frontier artificial-intelligence model developer to do an IPO, follows SpaceX's June offering, as investors jump at the chance for exposure to the fast-growing industry, even as the industry also faces mounting questions over the cost of developing and operating artificial intelligence models.

Trump's historic meeting with Xi, Putin headlines Asia trip
US President Donald Trump will cap his Asia trip on Thursday with an unprecedented meeting with Chinese and Russian counterparts Xi Jinping and Vladimir Putin, pressing his ambitions for nuclear arms control even as Beijing resists making the issue a centerpiece of the gathering.
The trilateral meeting ‌will bring together the leaders of the world's three largest nuclear powers for an unusual diplomatic gathering that could showcase their influence but is unlikely to produce major agreements, analysts say.

Sri Lanka Central Bank raises key policy rate, SRR citing high inflation, credit growth
Sri Lanka’s Central Bank raised its key monetary policy rate by 25 basis points on Friday (20) and increased commercial banks’ Statutory Reserve Ratio (SRR) by 1 percent in a surprise move citing higher inflation and credit growth.The Monetary Policy Board, at its meeting held Thursday (19), decided to increase the Overnight Policy Rate (OPR) by 25 basis points (bps) to 9.00%.

Budget 2027: ‘SL needs specificity on trade reform, IMF’: ODI
While Sri Lanka’s 2027 Budget demonstrates its effort to prioritise macro-economic stability, productivity, export promotion, investment, digitalisation and state capacity – the lack of specificity on trade integration, labour market reform, and the Sri Lankan government’s continued work with the IMF leave more to be desired, Overseas Development Institute Global (ODI) said in its review of the Budget.
Reference: https://tinyurl.com/mvumwsh8

Debt repayments 2028: ‘IMF follow-up programme would steady Sri Lanka’: Analysts
As Sri Lanka prepares to exit a $2.9 billion IMF programme early next year, analysts say a follow-up programme with the international lender to underpin the country's recent budget would help it weather volatile global energy costs, post stronger growth and prepare for debt repayments."A follow-on IMF programme could serve as a supportive policy anchor and help provide a financing backstop ⁠amid relatively volatile global conditions," said Jeremy Zook, a senior director at Fitch Ratings.

Sri Lanka must prove recovery is more than a cycle: Hosking
Hosking Partners LLP Founder and Portfolio Manager Jeremy Hosking said the London-based fund, encouraged by the 2027 Budget, would stay invested in Sri Lanka. He said it would make a substantially larger commitment only if the country proved its turnaround was secular rather than cyclical, a test he said entrenched resistance to change would make hard to pass.Sri Lanka accounts for about 2% of the fund’s global portfolio, spread across about 12 companies. The fund added to its holdings when the economy collapsed in 2022, consistent with the capital cycle approach Hosking helped pioneer in 1986. The approach holds that returns recover where capital has fled and competition has thinned, and fall where capital floods in. Those holdings have since risen sharply.

Hosking Partners ups Sri Lanka exposure with Rs. 1 b JAT stake
UK-based global equity investment manager Hosking Partners LLP has increased its exposure to Sri Lankan equities with the purchase of a 5.18% stake in JAT Holdings PLC for Rs. 1.05 billion. It bought the entire holding of the company’s second-largest shareholder, Falcon Trading Ltd.
Funds managed by Hosking Partners bought 27,077,498 shares at Rs. 38.8 each. Before the sale, Falcon Trading ranked second only to Aelian Gunawardene, who holds a controlling 63.63% stake in JAT.The firm is among the top 20 shareholders in John Keells Holdings, Aitken Spence, CT Holdings, Richard Pieris, Bukit Darah, Dialog Axiata, Tokyo Cement, Ceylon Guardian Investment Trust, Teejay Lanka and Lion Brewery. Its Sri Lankan equity portfolio was reported to exceed $ 60 million.

NSB Group delivers Rs 45.8bn operating profit in 9M 2026
National Savings Bank Group (NSB) sustained its core banking momentum during the first nine months of 2026, supported by stronger net interest income, strong growth in fee-based earnings and continued expansion in loans and advances. The Group’s net interest income rose 7.4% to Rs 69.1 billion, total operating income increased 3.6% to Rs 71.2 billion and net operating income grew 5.4% to Rs 75.3 billion. Group profit before tax amounted to Rs 34.7 billion, broadly in line with Rs 34.8 billion in the corresponding period of 2025, while profit after tax stood at Rs 20.7 billion.

Group total assets increased to Rs 1.92 trillion and Group equity rose 8.7% to Rs 139.05 Billion.

Anthropic becomes one of world's most valuable public companies in stock market debut
Anthropic has become one of the most valuable public companies in the world after its shares began trading on the stock market, taking its valuation to roughly $1.76 trillion (£1.34 trillion). The artificial intelligence (AI) company's Thursday debut on the Nasdaq stock exchange was a crucial test for the industry, given the huge amount of money being poured into advancing the technology.

Japan core inflation soars to highest this year as energy subsidy expiry pushes up consumer prices
Headline inflation came in at 2.3% compared with September’s 2.1%, while the so-called “core-core” inflation, which strips out prices of fresh food and energy, dipped slightly to 2.2% from 2.4% in the month before, government data released on Friday showed. Energy subsidies for households expired in September, exposing consumers to higher prices brought about by the Iran war. Energy prices climbed 2.2% in October, a sharp spike from the 0.6% decline in September. Gas prices jumped 5.8% compared to the 2.4% rise the month before.
